newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees London Club closing mid-April.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees London Club closing mid-April.

text.p: Russia will finish reconciling 50 percent of its debt to commercial bank creditors by the end of next week and close the entire London Club rescheduling deal in mid-April, a senior Finance Ministry official said on Friday.

"By the end of February Vneshekonombank's reconcilation office will send reconciliation statements to the creditors for a sum exceeding half the minimum necessary sum for closing the deal," Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov told Reuters.
The minimum necessary sum for closing the London Club rescheduling is $20 billion.
So far Russia has done reconciliations on over $2 billion of debt and by the end of February it will reconcile over $10 billion, Kasaynov said.
"By this we are confirming that London Club rescheduling will be done by mid-April," he said.
Russia agreed in 1995 with the London Club to reschedule $35 billion in debts inherited from the Soviet Union and interest arrears for up to 25 years.
